researchFindings: An unbuilt idea must be communicated to listeners who do not share the planner’s mental image.
A familiar work name may obscure the new idea’s own appeal and may invoke different examples for different generations or experiences.
The listener may form an analogy; the presenter should explain the actual distinctive experience and avoid relying on a title as the whole explanation.
The source permits comparison shorthand in suitable shared contexts; it does not forbid all comparison or analysis.
originalConcept.limitations: Auto-caption transcription errors are preserved. Do not reconstruct an unclear specific Mario example or treat this as exact human-approved wording.

candidateViewerQuestion: How can I explain an unbuilt game idea so listeners understand the actual player actions and choices without depending on a familiar work name?
distinctScope: Replace an ambiguous familiar-title summary with a visible player-action cycle.
Explain the distinctive constraint, choice and result in that cycle, within observed footage limits.
Check which shared assumptions the listener needs; use comparisons as supporting shorthand only when their scope is explicit.
outOfScope: Re-teaching game analysis and controlled tests from deconstruct-analyze-rebuild.
Re-teaching hierarchical outlines, job roles or reward catalogue planning.
Reusing historical funding allegations as current facts.
Copying or translating the full source lecture, guessing the unclear Mario example, or asserting listener test results without an actual test.
decisionReason: Full original concept plus eight related KO/EN scripts and the existing funding/evaluation video were directly compared. The candidate addresses new-game pitch communication and different listener associations. Existing analysis teaches observe/test/rebuild, hierarchy teaches containment and references, career introduces job roles, rewards plans a catalogue, and funding content critiques historical evaluation procedures. Their central questions, chapter claims and practical deliverables differ. Actual Korean title/description searches, four separate current English metadata dialogs and full related scripts support the decision; zero exact matches or title differences alone do not.
